chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said: Muath ibn Muslim narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Do not leave reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun' in seven places: in the two rak'at before Fajr, the two rak'at of midday (Dhuhr), two rak'at after Maghrib, two rak'at from the beginning of the night prayer, the two rak'at of Ihram, and Fajr when you begin the morning with it, and the two rak'at of Tawaf.

And in another report: that one should begin in all of these with 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and in the second rak'at with 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun', except in the two rak'at before Fajr, for one should begin with 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun', then recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in the second rak'at.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: Which prayers require reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Kafirun together according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi emphasizes the spiritual significance of Surah Al-Ikhlas and Al-Kafirun by prescribing their recitation in seven specific prayer units, highlighting their role in daily devotional practice. The variant narration clarifies the recitation order, notably reversing the sequence for the pre-dawn prayers to distinguish them from other times, reflecting the meticulous attention to ritual detail in Shia jurisprudence. This practice underscores the thematic connection between monotheism (Tawhid) and the rejection of shirk, central to the believer's daily worship.
